author_receipt.author: financial_integrity
author_receipt.receipt_reasoning: Authorizes actor/optional approval, normalizes and requires name, returns an existing case-insensitive normalized name even when the request has a different fee, otherwise inserts request-key ID with raw nullable fee; same-ID DB conflict replays by ID. Read-by-name has no transaction-held name lock or shown uniqueness guard. Negative/large fee accepted locally; order fee is frozen at checkout. Same-name/different-fee, concurrent distinct IDs and negative/extreme fee tests absent.

independent_source_reasoning.authorization_and_input: The handler loads the request's ActorUserId and derives the actor from the persisted user, optionally resolves manager approval, then calls AuthorizationPolicy.AuthorizeCommand for delivery_manage (DeliveryServiceHandlers.cs:28-40; ApprovalRegistry.cs:69-78). Name is normalized and empty name rejected (42-43). No fee sign or magnitude validation occurs in this method.
independent_source_reasoning.deduplication_and_write: It queries for matching normalized name and returns that existing DTO before considering the new request fee (45-47). Otherwise the database entity uses ID delivery-service-{RequestId} and copies FeePiastres directly (49-53), then saves (54-57). A DbUpdateException only replays by entity ID (59-64). The app model shown for DeliveryServices configures only the primary key (FalahDbContext.cs:318-320); migration creates Name as nvarchar(max), nullable FeePiastres as bigint and only a primary key on Id (20260904151353_AddOrderTaxSnapshotAndDeliveryServices.cs:39-53). No normalized-name uniqueness or fee check constraint is present in those examined model/migration sections. Thus distinct request IDs can conditionally insert duplicate normalized names under a read-then-insert race; whether deployment adds an external constraint was not tested.
independent_source_reasoning.money_workflow: This handler changes service configuration, not an order, cash drawer, treasury journal, or stock row. The active-service query returns FeePiastres unchanged (DeliveryQueryService.cs:24-26). CashierViewModel loads that list and passes the selected FeePiastres into CheckoutOrderRequest (CashierViewModel.Delivery.cs:80-93; CashierViewModel.Checkout.cs:348-361). CheckoutOrderHandler converts request.DeliveryFeePiastres directly to Money and carries it into the checkout plan (CheckoutOrderHandler.cs:65-73, 142-143); CheckoutRules.ComputePayableTotal adds fee and subtracts comp, then floors a negative result at zero (CheckoutRules.cs:35-39). Accordingly a negative stored service fee can flow through the ordinary cashier selection path unless rejected elsewhere; the inspected creation handler does not reject it. This is a configuration-entry path into the already-recorded checkout fee issue, not evidence that this configuration operation itself posts money.
independent_source_reasoning.counterevidence_and_limits: DeliveryDirectoryViewModel.SaveServiceAsync uses CashInput.TryParse and explicitly rejects parsed values below zero before creating/updating through that UI (DeliveryDirectoryViewModel.cs:180-208). That is useful for ordinary UI use but does not constrain direct authorized API requests or other clients. Handler authorization still gates delivery_manage or valid approval; this is not an authorization bypass. Order fee/total are handled from the checkout request and order data, so editing service configuration does not retroactively alter already-created orders (DeliveryServiceRequests.cs:3-10; source semantics in CheckoutOrderHandler). No live request, database, concurrent race or customer sale was executed.
independent_source_reasoning.finding_overlap: FIN-016 in Codex Work/Deep-Audit/MASTER_FINDINGS.json already covers the signed checkout delivery-fee path and its conditional payable/comp consequences. This review supports a catalog-ingress path into that same issue and the receipt's unconfirmed duplicate-name race lead; it does not create or recommend a separate duplicate FIN finding. FIN-003 concerns refunds and has no new counterevidence from this review; no disposition change is proposed.
independent_source_reasoning.receipt_accuracy: Source matches the receipt's core claims: actor/approval gate, name normalization/replay, raw nullable fee persistence, replay by same ID, and absence of displayed normalized-name uniqueness guard. The caller trace strengthens the financial relevance. The race consequence remains conditional and unexecuted.

review.review_verdict: SUBSTANTIVE_REVIEW_VERIFIED_IN_REVIEWER_OWNED_EVIDENCE; receipt reasoning corroborated with caller/migration/test cross-check. No shared class promotion performed.
review.finding_disposition: OVERLAP_WITH_FIN-016; configuration ingestion expands the same signed-fee path, not a separate finding. Retain the receipt's distinct-name concurrent create lead as a conditional configuration-integrity hypothesis pending policy/deployment and concurrency verification.
review.risk: If nonnegative delivery fees are intended, a delivery_manage-authorized direct API request can persist a negative service fee despite the cashier's ordinary management UI preventing it; the active fee is exposed unchanged and the cashier copies it into checkout. Financial effect depends on using that service and checkout request flow; no actual order or drawer/ledger movement was observed.
remaining_actions: Owner/product policy: confirm whether delivery service fee must be nonnegative and whether upper bounds are required.
If policy confirmed, add server-side sign/range validation to create and update handlers and regression tests for negative, extreme and nullable fee semantics; preserve valid zero/positive behavior.

Test same normalized name with different request IDs and fees and decide whether first-writer return or uniqueness/rejection is intended; if uniqueness is required, enforce it in persistent storage and test concurrent inserts.
Add end-to-end checkout test demonstrating service fee snapshot amount; current service tests do not assert it.
